title: Incident choiceboard and customer evidence kits — opt-in replay & verification guide
summary: Draft customer-facing choiceboard + evidence kit after the May 15 inference routing degradation. This doc is written for customers who want a concise status update on what we observed, a reproducible evidence package to verify their own tenant data, and a set of choices (replay, refund/credit, or opt-out) they can select. Intended to be used as a statuspage update + follow-up customer email with an attachment link to the evidence bundle.
impact: Between 2026-05-15 02:13 UTC and 2026-05-15 03:42 UTC some inference requests experienced elevated latencies and, for a subset of tenants, truncated streaming outputs. Approximate affected surface: 1.8% of total requests during the window; ~0.5% of premium-tier requests experienced truncated streaming where final tokens were missing. No data exfiltration detected. No billing data corruption detected (tokens recorded normally).
timeline:
Key timeline (UTC):
- 02:11: internal alert: upstream routing error rate increased (SRE)
- 02:13: first customer reports via support@ and Slack channel #cust-prod
- 02:20: automated rollback to last-known-good routing policy initiated (partially successful)
- 02:26: engineering identified cascade between regional routing and model variant fallback logic (routing policy mismatch)
- 02:35: partial mitigation deployed (soft-fail to fallback variant disabled for affected region)
- 02:50: streaming agent patch deployed to re-emit final chunk when detection triggered
- 03:01: SLO-targets still not fully met for high-concurrency tenants — throttles applied for noisy tenants
- 03:42: all mitigation steps completed; system returned to steady-state
- 04:10: monitoring validated no recurring regressions for 28 minutes and closed the active incident
technical_root_cause: Root cause: a regression in the routing policy state machine introduced in a recent rollout (PR #1792) changed the precedence order for 'regional capacity' vs 'model-variant-compatibility'. Under a transient capacity signal in us-west-2, requests were routed to a model variant with a streaming implementation mismatch for long-prompt sessions. That mismatch occasionally caused the streaming agent to drop the final chunk when a specific sequence of KV-cache eviction + variant swap occurred. The regression only manifested under high-concurrency prefix patterns. Contributing factors: insufficient integration test coverage for cross-region fallback, and monitoring alerts were noisy and masked the early signal.
mitigations:
Immediate mitigations performed:
- Rolled back the routing precedence change (rollback tag: rollback-2026-05-15-rp)
- Disabled automatic variant fallback for long-stream sessions in affected regions
- Deployed a hotfix to the streaming agent to detect and re-request final chunks on variant swap (hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1798)
- Applied temporary rate-limiting to noisy tenants to protect tail latency while root cause investigation continued
Longer-term mitigations planned:
- Add integration test covering cross-region fallback + streaming (in test-grid)
- Add a circuit-breaker to disallow variant swap mid-stream for >2s operations
- Improve alert signal-to-noise by surfacing per-region variant-swap rates in the console
verification_and_evidence:
What we will provide to customers:
1) A downloadable evidence kit (link will be posted on status) containing:
   - anonymized request traces (per-tenant when available) covering the window 2026-05-15T02:00–04:30Z
   - server-side streaming logs and agent-level debug for affected host IDs (redacted keys)
   - a short reproducible script (curl + minimal prompt) customers can run to confirm their tenant behavior against a preserved snapshot endpoint
2) Verification steps for customers who want to validate outcomes themselves:
   - Step A: Retrieve trace bundle (link) and open claims.csv (contains request_id, tenant_id, timestamp, status)
   - Step B: Run the included replay script with your tenant token (REPLAY MODE will hit a read-only snapshot, safe for customers)
   - Step C: Compare your observed token counts to claims.csv; instructions and a small python comparator are included in the kit
3) We will also provide a signed integrity file (SHA256) for the evidence bundle so customers can validate no tampering.
Notes: For privacy we will only include tenant-specific traces when the customer opts in; otherwise we provide aggregate anonymized data.
customer_options_and_next_steps:
Choiceboard for affected customers (we will include this as a short form in the status email):
Option 1: Opt-in to replay + verification (recommended for customers who need proof for internal audits). We will run a safe read-only replay and give results plus the evidence kit.
Option 2: Request a credit for the impacted window (calculated pro-rata on total tokens during the window). No replay required.
Option 3: Do nothing (no action) — we will flag your tenant as 'observed but no action requested' and close the customer-facing thread.
How to choose: reply to this email with one of the option codes (REPLAY / CREDIT / NOACTION). If you request REPLAY, please include any request_ids or example prompts you want validated.
Expected timelines: Replay & evidence delivery within 48 hours of opt-in; credit issuance within 5 business days after verification (if chosen).
faq:
Q: Was customer data exposed? A: No evidence of data exfiltration. All logs included in the kit are redacted and shared only with customer consent.
Q: Will this happen again? A: We have implemented immediate rollbacks and a targeted hotfix. Longer-term changes (integration tests and breakers) are scheduled and tracked in JIRA-INC-4283.
Q: Do I need to rotate keys? A: No. There is no indication of key compromise tied to this event.
Q: Can I opt out of replays? A: Yes — select NOACTION.
Q: Who do I contact for escalation? A: Reply to support@redwood.com with subject line 'INC-4283 — Customer Escalation' and include your tenant id.
compensation_policy_summary: Short: eligible commercial customers may receive a token-based credit for the impacted window. Credits are prorated and automatically applied once a request is acknowledged. We are also offering replay and evidence for audit needs at no charge. Details: credits calculated on billed tokens within the window; micro-transactional customers can choose a 1-month service credit in lieu of token credit. Finance and legal to approve high-value custom compensation requests (contact: finance-ops@redwood.com).

Please reply with one of the option codes below: REPLAY, CREDIT, or NOACTION. If you select REPLAY, include any request IDs you want validated.

Link to evidence kit (read-only): <statuspage link>

Thanks,
Asha on behalf of Redwood Inference Support
delivery_plan:
How we'll send this:
1) Post a concise statuspage notice with a short TL;DR and a link to this choiceboard + evidence kit (statuspage entry marked 'customer-actionable')
2) Send targeted emails to the tenant owners of affected commercial customers (use the support CRM filter)
3) Open a ticket for each customer who opts in (label: INC-4283-replay) and attach the customer-specific evidence bundle after consent
